newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end higher taking foreign lead.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end higher taking foreign lead.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended sharply up in line with weaker foreign markets on Thursday while the crown followed the generally weaker dollar and softened against the mark.
"All European markets are weaker today, the U.S. market too. The crown is also weaker," one analyst said.
Six month T-bill rate rose six basis points to 4.15 percent and the ten year bond yield climbed ten basis points to 7.22 percent.
Centre Party leader Olof Johansson said he would stand for reelection which pleased the market.
Dealers said his resignation would have caused political uncertainty about the party's informal alliance with the minority Social Democratic government.
The immediate market focus on Friday was U.S. producer price and retail sales. The Swedish budget and March Cosumer Price Index due out on April 15 were also in focus.
March CPI is expected to show a rise of 0.4 percent month-on-month and a fall of 0.4 percent year-on-year, according to a Reuter survey.
The crown softened to 4.4805 against the mark from 4.4745 late Wednesday. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
